children: Shares of Jupiter Neurosciences fell after it disclosed a notice from Nasdaq that the stock exchange intends to delist Jupiter's shares, citing the company's non-compliance with a rule setting a minimum total value for its listed securities.
The stock fell 18%, to $3.42, in after-hours trading Friday, after closing down 15%, at $4.18. Through the close, shares had lost 95% of their value this year.

Nasdaq notified Jupiter on Thursday that it missed an Aug. 25 deadline to regain compliance with a rule requiring listed securities to have a total market value of at least $35 million. Nasdaq first notified Jupiter of its noncompliance and set the deadline in February.
The company's market capitalization was recently around $6 million based on its Thursday closing price of $4.89, according to FactSet.

Jupiter said that it would appeal Nasdaq's determination by requesting a hearing before the Nasdaq Hearings Panel, and that it expects the request to lead to a stay of any further action. It said it was considering all options available to regain compliance with the rule.
The company separately said that it regained compliance with a separate rule requiring it to maintain a minimum closing bid price of $1.00 a share for 10 consecutive business days.
